extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys facing or advising on USPTO reciprocal discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO final order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state supreme court suspension; describes procedural steps, required notices, the basis for suspension, and respondent obligations. Useful for producing or evaluating USPTO discipline orders and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state authority when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted state authority (action brought pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and serves a Notice and Order by certified mail; the respondent has an opportunity to file a response within forty (40) days opposing imposition of identical discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If no valid reason negating the presumption is shown, reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate violation citation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order ties USPTO disciplinary action to the specific regulatory predicate identified in the Complaint; the existence of the state discipline satisfying the cited regulation supports imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural notice and response requirements (service and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. provided) notifying Respondent and providing an opportunity to file a response within forty (40) days to oppose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service by certified mail with proof of receipt and a defined response period (40 days) are required procedural steps; responses may assert defects in prior proceedings or invoke statutory/regulatory exceptions to reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for determination — genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director determines whether a genuine issue of material fact exists under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d); absent such an issue, reciprocal discipline as imposed by the state is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not establish any of the § 11.24(d)(1) bases or otherwise raise a genuine issue of material fact, the Office will adopt the state's discipline (as occurred here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension terms and reinstatement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO for sixty (60) days, commencing on the date of the Final Order; respondent remains suspended until the OED Director grants a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies both the fixed suspension period and the procedural requirement that reinstatement requires a petition under § 11.60; the suspension may thus continue beyond the stated period until the petition is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette (content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, identifying the practitioner by name, residence, and registration number, stating that the suspension is predicated upon suspension by a state authority, and citing the state court order and the specific rules violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes a model Notice of Suspension that lists the practitioner's name, registration number, the state order citation and date, and the specific state professional conduct rules found violated (example text provided in the order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the Respondent is admitted, to courts where the Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory inter-jurisdictional notice ensures other jurisdictions and courts are informed of the USPTO action and the factual/reason basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order does not restate § 11.58, it imposes the regulatory duties that apply during suspension (e.g., client notice, file transfer, and other administrative duties specified in § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Number(s) and USPTO electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative disassociation is a remedy to prevent the suspended practitioner's continued electronic practice before the Office during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: KRPC 1.6(a) — confidentiality violation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of Kansas found a violation of Kansas Rules of Professional Conduct § 1.6(a) when Respondent revealed confidential information to court services officers in a client's case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing client confidential information to third parties (court services officers) can constitute a violation that supports disciplinary action by state and reciprocal action by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: KRPC 3.3(a)(1) — candor to the tribunal (misleading about prosecutor's attendance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court found Respondent violated KRPC 3.3(a)(1) by leading the district court to believe that the prosecutor declined to come to court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misleading a tribunal about another party's actions or intentions can constitute an ethical violation; such findings are incorporated into the USPTO Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: KRPC 3.3(d) — candor at ex parte hearing (failure to disclose material facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court found a violation of KRPC 3.3(d) where, at an ex parte hearing, Respondent failed to inform the district court of all material facts known to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose material facts in ex parte or other tribunal contexts is an ethical violation supporting discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: KRPC 8.4(c) — professional conduct involving dishonesty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kansas courts concluded Respondent violated KRPC 8.4(c) when he made dishonest statements to a tribunal about the status of his client's sobriety, told the court the prosecutor declined to go to court, and drafted a journal entry that contained false information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dishonest statements to a tribunal and drafting or submitting false documents are grounds for significant disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: KRPC 8.4(d) — professional misconduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kansas courts found Respondent violated KRPC 8.4(d) when he drafted a journal entry that he knew contained inaccurate and false information for the court's signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating or facilitating false court records that prejudice the administration of justice is an ethical violation cited in the Notice and supporting reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and scope of the Notice of Suspension (challenge and determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent asserted a 'minor inaccuracy' in the proposed Notice of Suspension regarding a finding under KRPC 3.3(c); the Office concluded the proposed Notice was accurate because the Kansas Supreme Court did not sustain a violation of 3.3(c) but did sustain other 3.3 violations referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a respondent challenges the accuracy of the proposed notice, the Office reviews the underlying state order to determine which specific findings were sustained and ensures the Official Gazette notice accurately reflects sustained findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for public availability of disciplinary decisions (FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs readers to the public repository for disciplinary decisions, supporting transparency and public notice as part of disciplinary practice.
